audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].side read 'Skill' while content win[6] read 'Kassadin' — a cross-layer disagreement on the last row, and phases[6].why described Diana diving.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s with escalating repeat cost; at two-plus items with the mana to spam it, and Void Stone cutting Diana's magic damage, the last row belongs to Kassadin. The packet levelChart and content whys[6] both say Kassadin.
audit.corrected: phases[6].side moved to Kassadin (win[6] already correct) and the why rewritten to describe him winning it.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named no cooldown and treated the spike list as Diana-only.
audit.why: Diana: E at 3 (22s rank 1), R at 6 (100/90/80). Kassadin's real spike is Riftwalk rank 3 at 2s.
audit.corrected: Spikes now name Lunar Rush, Moonfall and the rank-3 Riftwalk at 2s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never used Void Stone, Null Sphere, Nether Blade or Force Pulse and had zero sequencing cues (packet defect).
audit.why: Void Stone reduces the magic damage Diana's entire kit deals. Null Sphere (650 range, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7) shields magic damage specifically, so it covers one Q, not the dash-string. Force Pulse charges from spells cast near him — Diana's own Q/W/E feed it — then fires a 400-range slowing cone on a 21s cooldown. Nether Blade is a 7s auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the burst tell rather than any cast. Riftwalk is a 500-range teleport at 5/3.5/2s with escalating mana cost on repeats.
audit.corrected: All four abilities named with their numbers, and step-up advice keyed to his blink and shield cooldowns.

audit.why: Riftwalk 5/3.5/2, Null Sphere 9-7, Force Pulse 21-17, Moonfall 100/90/80.

audit.whatIsWrong: content late said 'Void Staff/Rabadon's territory' with the packet flagging 'Void Staff' as a suspect name, and wants.foe[2] called Void Stone a build.
audit.why: Void Staff is a real item he buys; Void Stone is his passive, magic damage reduction. The page conflated them.
audit.corrected: Void Staff kept as the item, Void Stone used correctly as the passive, and wants.foe[2] reworded to item scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); phases[5].why claimed 'chunks half bars' with no source.
audit.why: The bullet titles promise disengage-punishing and wave-chasing, not the generic trade lines; the magnitude is unsourced.
audit.corrected: Both bullets rewritten to their own titles; the magnitude replaced with the Null Sphere shield cooldown.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Kassadin

edits.before: Late Diana dives: E the carry through the front line, R the clump that collapses, and reset through the wreckage.
edits.after: Two items in, Riftwalk is a 2-second blink he can spam — he leaves your Moonfall slow behind and picks the fight later.

edits.before: Q the wave's edge and his face in one arc — the crescent farms and pokes at once; learn the curve's sweet spot.
edits.after: Q the wave's edge and his face in one arc — Kassadin has no level 1 damage and his Q is only 650 range.

edits.before: W shield-trade window: orbs absorb his poke and pay it back on the three-hit passive.
edits.after: Pale Cascade orbs outlast his 650-range Null Sphere; trade when he steps up to last-hit.

edits.before: E pull joins... no — your dash threat begins: Q-mark into E reset chases are live; trade on every landed crescent.
edits.after: Lunar Rush online at 3 and he has no escape until 6 — Q-mark, dash, three-hit string, and repeat on every landed arc.

edits.before: Mark-dash trades on cooldown — Q, E to the mark, passive three-hit, walk. The lane respects the curve now.
edits.after: Every spell you cast near him charges Force Pulse — burst him from the mark, do not stand in his 400-range cone.

edits.before: Moonfall online — the R pull turns any clumped trade into your fight. With jungle help it's a guaranteed flip.
edits.after: Moonfall online — his Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and costly, so pull him before he can afford a second blink out.

edits.before: First item spike: the mark-dash combo chunks half bars and the reset chains through waves.
edits.after: First item: Q-mark into E — his Null Sphere shield is 9s and covers one arc, not the string.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Check it before every step-up. - W Pale Cascade is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3: the lane is decided before it reaches rank 3. - Null Sphere is 9s at rank 1 and only shields magic damage. - Force Pulse is 21s once charged. - Your Moonfall is 100s; spend it on him, not a wave.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Pale Cascade eats his Null Sphere and the third sphere adds shield — orbs up before you step in.

edits.before: Q through the wave onto his chest, E the mark, three-hit string, walk — the phase trade he answers after you've left.
edits.after: Riftwalk costs more mana each repeat — dash to the Moonlight mark right after his first blink, before he can afford another.

edits.before: Kassadin spends Riftwalk early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Once he blinks in, Moonfall drags him back onto you and the string finishes him.

edits.before: That’s Kassadin’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: At 6 his Riftwalk is 5s and mana-thin — take the fight you set up, not his.

edits.before: Dashing onto an unmarked target with W down — Diana without the reset or the shield is a melee mage donating proximity.
edits.after: Every spell you throw near him charges Force Pulse — chasing through his wave hands him the 400-range cone and the slow.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to rank 3 Riftwalk, blinking out of every Moonfall, and letting Void Stone eat your magic damage.

edits.before: Ahead, phase harder: zone Kassadin with crescent threat, dive the river fights, and R every clump — fed Diana makes grouping illegal.
edits.after: Ahead, deny his farm: Riftwalk mana costs punish a behind Kassadin, so shove, take plates, and dive him with your jungler before rank 3.

edits.before: Farm the sweet spots and shield-trade — your early is sturdier than assassin stereotypes. Every landed Q is a banked dash.
edits.after: Farm at max Q range and trade behind orbs — Kassadin is mana-poor with a 650-range Q, so every landed arc is a free dash.

edits.before: First item onward, chain the phases: mark-dash the contacts, R the river clumps, and reset through whatever groups.
edits.after: First item onward the clock is his: force skirmishes and dives with your jungler before Riftwalk hits rank 3 and 2 seconds.

edits.before: Level 3 mark-dash sets the pattern; level 6 adds the pull; first item makes phases lethal.
edits.after: Level 3 arms Lunar Rush; level 6 adds Moonfall; his rank 3 Riftwalk at 2s ends yours.

edits.before: Carry through the dive — mark, dash, pull, delete; your R turns their teamfight spacing into a suggestion.
edits.after: Carry by ending it early — mark, dash, three-hit, and use Moonfall on him the moment he blinks into your team.

edits.before: You are the dive: E through the front line onto their carry, R the collapse, and let the resets carry you out famous.
edits.after: Late this flips: his Riftwalk is 2s and Void Stone cuts your magic damage, so fight only with your team and Moonfall the blink.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the weakest level 1-5 mid laners in the game — no mana, a clunky short Q, and no wave clear. All-in him relentlessly with Q-mark into E whenever he steps up to farm; he has almost no answer. Deny his CS to slow his mana problems even further. This is your best window in the entire matchup, so don't waste it playing passive.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest level 1-5 mid laners in the game — mana-hungry, a 650-range Q, and no wave clear. All-in him with Q-mark into E whenever he steps up to farm. His only trade is Nether Blade, an auto-attack reset on a 7s cooldown: the wind-up is your cue to step out, not the cast. Deny his CS and this window is your whole matchup.

edits.before: By level 6 you still have the edge since his Riftwalk range and mana pool are limited, but every point he puts into R and every mana item narrows your advantage. Keep forcing skirmishes and dives with jungle before he hits 2-3 items. Avoid long protracted lanes — the later it goes, the more his scaling closes the gap and eventually flips it.
edits.after: By level 6 you still have the edge: Riftwalk is 500 range, 5s and expensive at rank 1, so pull him with Moonfall the moment he blinks in. Every rank in R cuts that to 3.5s then 2s, so force skirmishes and dives with your jungler before he hits 2-3 items. The later it goes, the more his scaling closes the gap and flips it.

edits.before: Once Kassadin reaches Void Staff/Rabadon's territory he becomes a snowballing burst mage who can Riftwalk-flash onto your backline faster than you can React, and his stacked magic resist shred makes him hit as hard as you do. If the game reaches this point your early lead needs to have already ended it — don't try to out-scale him in a straight late-game fight.
edits.after: Once Kassadin has Void Staff and Rabadon's he becomes a burst mage who blinks onto your backline faster than you can react, and Void Stone still keeps cutting the magic damage you answer with. If the game reaches this point your early lead needs to have already ended it — do not try to out-scale him in a straight late-game fight.

edits.before: Survive to late game where Void Stone build takes over
edits.after: Survive to late game where his item scaling takes over
